summary: The AddVoter receipt landed a third execution-grounded finding, and I recorded it with its limits rather than as a bare claim. All three declared comparisons hold and are complete: the server added through the exported API appears in the configuration with suffrage Voter in both cases, so the staging behaviour its comment describes is absent; on the single-voter cluster (two voters, one living, quorum 2) the subsequent apply came back as not-leader with the node a Candidate and no leader anywhere in the cluster; RemoveServer for the same unreachable server also came back as not-leader with the configuration still listing two voters, so there is no in-band repair; and the control on the three-voter cluster kept its leader, applied successfully and removed the server cleanly, which is what makes the single-voter outcome a consequence of the quorum relation rather than of the operation being broken. I paired the behaviour with the two published contracts it collides with — the bootstrap advice to start with a single voter and add the rest with AddVoter, and the AddVoter comment promising a staging step — and with the one real escape route, RecoverCluster, so the counterevidence states plainly that the cluster is not unrecoverable, only unrecoverable in band, and that the staging text may simply be stale with AddNonvoter as the intended replacement (which moves the defect to the contract rather than removing the behavioural half). I promoted the two knowledge entries the account rests on, marked the question explained, and kept the limitations honest: two shapes probed, the added server never started, single-process in-memory execution, and the claim scoped to this snapshot's code and comments. The run now holds three asserted findings — the startup replay blocking NewRaft, the nonvoter acknowledgement satisfying VerifyLeader's voter quorum, and this membership change stranding a single-voter cluster — plus two refuted suspicions whose negative evidence is retained.
